### Chapter 25.

In the fourth year of Jehoiakim <note>original: "Ioachim." King of Judah (c. 609–598 BC)</note>, which is the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the word came to the prophet Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah. *From the days of Pope Leo the Sicilian <note>Pope Leo II (r. 682–683), who was born in Sicily and known for his learning</note>, whose sermons are remembered, as if he were another King Josiah of Judah <note>Josiah was a reforming king of Judah who rediscovered the Book of the Law</note>, until the time of Pope Paschal <note>Likely Pope Paschal II (r. 1099–1118), whose reign was marked by the Investiture Controversy and conflict with the Holy Roman Empire</note>, the people of the Church were frequently warned to leave the path of death and to hold fast to the path of life without laziness. Otherwise, the Lord was going to send the King of Babylon <note>In Joachim's prophetic system, the "King of Babylon" often represents the coming Antichrist or a tyrannical secular ruler who punishes a corrupt Church</note> to destroy them.*

->ON THE PROPHET JEREMIAH<-

To the [King] of Tyre, and to the King of Sidon, etc. <note>original: "Tyri, & ad Regem Sidonis &c." Joachim is interpreting Jeremiah 27:3, where Jeremiah is commanded to send bonds and yokes to various kings.</note> **Moreover, I have given him even the beasts of the field, that they might serve him.** <note>Jeremiah 27:6.</note> Bonds and chains are signs of captivity, and they are placed on the neck as a symbol of subjection. In this passage, the King of Tyre corresponds, through spiritual agreement, to the *King of Sicily and his land*; the King of Sidon corresponds to *certain secular princes and their lands established in the Roman regions.* The *beasts of the field* are either the *Saracens* <note>The Muslim forces then occupying parts of the Mediterranean and Holy Land.</note> or the *Patarenes* <note>A term used in the Middle Ages for various heretical groups, most notably the Cathars.</note>. The King of Edom corresponds to the *Greek regions*—that is, the province of *Constantinople* itself and its neighboring nations. The King of Moab corresponds to the *Lombards* <note>Inhabitants of Northern Italy, often in conflict with the Papacy and Empire.</note> and their lands; the King of Ammon corresponds to the *Tuscans* and their lands. These five provinces are to be handed over and liberated even to the **Empire**, <note>The Holy Roman Empire.</note> on account of the service they have done for the Lord and for the purpose of creating a scourge <note>A divine punishment or "whip" used to discipline the Church.</note> for the Church. But at the suggestion of certain doctors and pontiffs in the Church, they busy themselves by departing from other *provinces*. Thus it follows:

Indeed, as for the fact that Shemaiah the Nehelamite <note>A false prophet in the biblical book of Jeremiah who sent letters to Jerusalem opposing Jeremiah's counsel.</note> wrote books and sent them to Jerusalem prophesying falsely—whom the Lord did not send—he signifies those who cause **cardinals and bishops to trust in falsehood, and stir them up to persecute the prophets and teachers of the Lord**, lest they expose any of the coming affliction against them. 

Truly, because Shemaiah, as the instigator of evils, is rejected: it is destined that in his offspring the end shall be brought upon those who give wicked counsel, and speak evil against the prince of the state <note>original: "principi reipublicæ." ### Chapter 30. ###

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying: "Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Write for yourself—that is, create a record for the memory and caution of those to come—all the words that I have spoken to you, in a book." This is the literal sense. Spiritually, "to write" is to preach in the book of human hearts. *Prophetic men are to be raised up in the Church, so that they may preach the words of the Lord among all Christian people, and convert them to the land of religion and peace, that they may confidently possess it in the observance of penance. And this is spoken to Israel and to Judah—that is to say, the Greeks and the Latins, or certainly the monastics and the clergy.* <note>original: "Græcos scilicet & Latinos." Joachim frequently interprets the biblical division of the Northern and Southern Kingdoms as a prophecy of the schism between the Greek Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches.</note> For thus says the Lord: "We have heard a voice of terror: there is dread, and there is no peace." *Weak hearts, once troubled, are thereafter rendered fearful and doubtful; for this reason, they mistake peace for strength, and security for terror. Nevertheless, some are rebuked, so that they might cast off fear and set their hearts toward believing the words of the Lord.* Ask and see: *learn and understand, does a male give birth—that is, does he labor? Far from it. The negligent and the weak are condemned.* "Why then have I seen every man's hand upon his loins, like a woman in labor?" *...[they] apply themselves [to loins], and waste away in carnal works. When they fail to be perfect and robust men, one gives birth in the spirit, not in the flesh; and they ought to have the shining faces of a [clear] conscience, not blackened by jaundice.* <note>original: "aurugine denigratas." Literally "blackened by the gold-sickness" (jaundice), here used metaphorically for a guilty or sickly conscience.</note> Woe

...and the house of Judah, *the Church of the Greeks and the Latins, with the seed of men and the seed of beasts,* <note>Jeremiah 31:27. Joachim interprets this "seed" as the spread of different types of religious teaching.</note> with doctrine that both strengthens the learned and builds up the unlearned. The **seed of man** is spiritual understanding; the **seed of the beast** is historical understanding. Or perhaps this designates the teachers as the "men," and signifies the listeners as the "livestock." *And just as I have watched over them for evil, so I will watch over them for good.* <note>Jeremiah 31:28</note>

Note here that the first "watch" is necessary for correction; the second is voluntary, for endurance. A proverbial expression meaning children suffer for their parents' actions. Joachim identifies the "sour grape" as the difficulty of the Old Testament Law.</note> because the children, being as yet imperfect, were in no way able to bear the hardness and bitterness of the Law. # ABBOT JOACHIM ON [JEREMIAH]

...for a time and times they groan under captivity. However, as it is said that there shall not be lacking a man from the seed of Jonadab, but that they shall stand forever in the sight of the Lord, it seems that the Cistercian Order <note>The Cistercian Order, a strict reform of Benedictine monasticism founded in 1098, was seen by Joachim as the vanguard of a new, spiritual age of the Church</note> is destined to endure until the end of the age.

### Chapter XXXVI.

<margin>Baruch 1.</margin>
Furthermore, the fact that Baruch wrote the revealed words of the Lord in the volume of a book from the mouth of Jeremiah must be referred to the future heralds of the Gospel. These heralds will preach publicly in the "book of human hearts," which will keep hidden within themselves the utterances concerning the misery and ruin of the world. <margin>Matthew 9.</margin> But because the leaders of the people, the high priests and the scribes—like old wineskins unable to contain the utterances of a new life—turn with all their deceits toward destroying the scroll. They act as if these heralds do not discourse fully on the Trinity, but rather cause confusion regarding its "quantity" <note>This likely refers to the theological conflict between Joachim and Peter Lombard; Joachim accused Lombard of creating a "quaternity" (four parts) instead of a Trinity by emphasizing the divine essence as a fourth thing</note>. With a scribe’s knife, they contemptuously cut away the opinions of any doctor of the church who is "knowledgeable in his own eyes."

The King indeed "was sitting in his winter house, and a brazier full of coals was set before him" <note>Referring to King Jehoiakim burning Jeremiah's scroll in Jeremiah 36:22-23</note>. When this passage has been fulfilled in history, it will then be better explained. <margin>John 18.</margin> For it is to come to pass that Peter, the Supreme Pontiff, shall sit by the coals because of the cold of the imminent winter. In this winter, zeal for God will grow cold, even according to knowledge, and the spirit of truth will be extinguished in spiritual men. <margin>Matthew 2. Matthew 27.</margin> But what if, because of the disturbance of Herod—another supreme and proud pontiff—Jesus flees, the star disappears, and the Magi evade him? In the earthquake that occurred... <note>original: "In terremotu facto" — the text ends mid-sentence, to be continued on the next page</note>

<summary>Joachim interprets the burning of Jeremiah's scroll as a prophecy of future church leaders (the "old wineskins") rejecting the spiritual teachings of the "new life." He uses the imagery of the "winter house" and Peter by the coals to predict a period of spiritual coldness and corruption in the papacy.</summary>

### Chapter 36

<margin>Baruch 1</margin>
Furthermore, the fact that Baruch wrote the revealed words of the Lord from the mouth of Jeremiah in the volume of a book is to be referred to the future heralds of the Gospel. These heralds will preach publicly in the "book of human hearts," and they shall hide within themselves <note>or "preserve among themselves"</note> the utterances concerning the misery and ruin of the world. 
<margin>Matthew 9</margin>
But because the princes of the people, the high priests, and the scribes—acting like **old wineskins** <note>A reference to the parable in Matthew 9:17; these leaders are too rigid to hold the new "wine" of spiritual revelation</note>—are not able to grasp the utterances of a new life, they turn with all their deceits to destroying the volume. They act as if these heralds do not fully explain the Trinity, but rather confound it by the sheer quantity of their words; and with the scribe’s penknife—by the judgment of some doctor who is a "know-it-all" <note>original: "scioli," meaning a person with superficial or prideful knowledge</note> in his own eyes—they cut the scroll away, despising it.

But what if, on account of the disturbance caused by **Herod** <margin>Matthew 2, Matthew 27</margin>—acting as another supreme and proud pontiff—Jesus flees, the star disappears, and the Magi evade? <margin>Isaiah 30.</margin> **Isaiah** says: *The strength of Pharaoh shall be to your confusion, and trust in the shadow of Egypt to your disgrace.* <note>original: "Erit vobis fortitudo Pharaonis in confusionem & fiducia vmbræ AEgypti in ignominia"; quoting Isaiah 30:3</note> For the weakness of human distrust has this quality: it trusts more in man than in God; and therefore, by a just judgment, it collapses from the very source where it hopes for help. Certainly, if we turn our eyes to the root of this evil, the **Church**—founded upon the humble Christ—ought not to think proudly or loftily, but rather fear that if it gapes after temporal riches, the wind might eventually carry them away like dust. For things are not given from abundance for pride, but for use; and therefore, he who is suddenly ended is built up in vain. 

In the time of the Apostles, the Church was sufficiently meager; but the heavy anguish of the **martyrs** who followed represents under how great a danger they stood. Teachers and confessors were bound and delivered to death and prison under the opening of the **third seal** <note>original: "signaculi tertij"; Joachim of Fiore (c. 1135–1202) famously divided history into seven periods corresponding to the Seven Seals of Revelation</note>. And in the fourth place, the reader’s skill should observe that the **Mahometan sect** <note>original: "secta Mahumetica"; Joachim viewed the rise of Islam as the fourth great tribulation of the Church</note> polluted spiritual virgins who had been terrified.

## ON JEREMIAH THE PROPHET

<page-num>371</page-num>

...clerical <note>original: "calis"; likely completing "clericalis" (clerical)</note> order, having expanded during times of peace, grown thick with resources, and become fattened by idleness, may not kick back <note>original: "recalcitret"; a biblical reference to Deuteronomy 32:15, where the people grow wealthy and turn against God</note>. Instead, what is superfluous should be given to the poor, and not to famous men or to the giants building the Tower of Babylon <margin>Gen. 11.</margin> <note>A reference to the Tower of Babel, symbolizing human pride and the confusion of tongues</note>. 

Attend, all of you. Gold was offered to Christ <margin>Mat. 2.</margin> so that by its help he might flee into Egypt; myrrh, that he might undergo the cross <note>original: "patibulum"; literally a yoke or gallows, referring here to the instrument of the Crucifixion</note>; and frankincense, so that he might praise God—not so that he might rebel against Herod, or be a burden to Pharaoh, nor to devote himself to luxuries and the enticements of gluttony, nor to be found ignorant and ungrateful for the benefits he received. 

Modern vicars of the Savior <note>A term for the Popes and high-ranking clergy who claim to act in Christ's place</note> neglect the frankincense, they neglect the myrrh, and they seek only gold, so that like Lady Babylon <margin>Apc. 17.</margin> <note>The "Whore of Babylon" from the Book of Revelation, representing a corrupt and worldly city or church</note> they may mix their drink in a golden cup and infect all their other followers with their own abomination. 

I believe Daniel discussed such men when he said: *When you shall see the abomination of desolation standing in the holy place: let him who reads understand* <margin>Dan. 9.</margin> <margin>Matt. 24.</margin>. The holy place is the Church, sanctified by the blood of Christ; the abomination is an unclean prelate <note>A high-ranking church official, such as a bishop or abbot</note> who desolates the throne of Solomon <note>A symbol of the seat of wisdom and divine judgment</note> by dragging away gold and destroying the ivory—which represents the purity of mind and flesh—while tearing apart prayers and works with his own hands. 

This man stands there because of his hunger for status; he does not read the holy scriptures, but rather fables, nor does he understand the miseries caused by his own arrogance. The day will come—indeed, it has already come—when the occupant of that seat <note>original: "assessor"; one who sits in a position of authority</note> shall fall backward at the bite of the twisted serpent, once the horses' hooves of the worldly powers have been wounded <note>This imagery draws on the prophecy in Genesis 49:17, where a serpent bites a horse's heels so the rider falls</note>.

Here it should be noted that your son, O Prince, represents the part of the secular princes or the pontiffs, toward Henry, of the church...

### Chapter 47

<image-desc>Ornate woodcut initial letter 'A' set within a square frame decorated with floral and foliate motifs.</image-desc> **TO MOAB.** <note>The Moabites, ancient neighbors of Israel, are used here as a code for the Byzantine Greeks.</note> The **Moabites** are the **Greeks**, whom the Lord indicates are to be devastated; and its **horn** <note>In biblical prophecy, a "horn" represents power or imperial authority.</note> signifies their empire, which is to be cut off from the nations of the Latin Empire. **Kiriathaim** is captured, which refers to the province of **Constantinople**. **Heshbon** as well, and other cities, are churches against which I have no doubt the destroyers will ascend, because the Greeks have acted deceitfully—holding the name of Christ, but corrupting the faith with errors. For this reason, **Moab** is put to shame by **Chemosh**, its idols; <note>Chemosh was the national god of Moab; here it represents the "idolatrous" theological errors of the Greeks.</note> and thus the glorious staff of the Greeks shall be broken.

This refers to the *Filioque* controversy, the major theological split between the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches over the origin of the Holy Spirit.</note>—proving this by their works and nesting in the highest opening of the cleft, announcing it to the other faithful. But the **pride of Moab** has been heard; he is exceedingly proud, scorning to return to the faith of ecclesiastical truth. *For the weeping of Jazer I will weep for you, O vineyard of Sibmah:* truly the **Latin Church** weeps for the **Greeks** as they waste away in the dregs of their errors, because they do not convert and live. Yet their captivity shall still be converted to the Roman faith.

Certainly, if one person presided over the commonwealth, and if the Christian people served God under him 
<margin>1 Corinthians 10</margin>
as a preeminent leader, the **Ship of Peter** <note>A traditional metaphor for the Catholic Church, depicting the Pope as the successor to the fisherman Peter, navigating the world's storms.</note> would not easily suffer such loss. But while he is to be exalted: let his successor take heed in time, lest—by thinking that the pontiffs fix the prow of their hope more firmly in Christian kings—the stern of the Roman chapter be shattered by the **German prince** <note>original: "Alemanici principis," referring to the Holy Roman Emperor, whose power frequently clashed with the Papacy.</note>. For this must happen, whether the world wishes it or not: that the strong members of the Church be gnawed upon, that pontifical pride fall, and that the ecclesiastical focus on temporal riches be diminished. And due to this sharing in the **Babylonian cup** <note>A biblical image for the intoxicating and corrupting influence of worldly power and sin.</note>, and because of the ruin of the Roman Empire, **Jeremiah** <note>The biblical prophet, whose warnings to Jerusalem are applied here to the Church.</note> advises the future men of the Gospel to retreat from the midst of the Babylon of the Chaldeans, lest they become sharers in the imminent eternal or temporal punishment. Indeed, **Peter** <note>Representing the Papacy.</note> must be led where he does not wish to go, 
<margin>John 21</margin>
and the Roman clergy or the pontifical order must be restricted. And lest **John and James** <note>Likely representing different orders or branches of the Church hierarchy.</note> perhaps chatter all the more that the care of souls was committed to them: since the religious and the **Greeks** <note>Referring to the Eastern Church, which Joachim often includes in his vision of universal tribulation and eventual reconciliation.</note> will lay down their lives for those souls, they too will not be able to avoid tasting the cup of the empire:

Finally, because Jeremiah writes the book concerning the evils coming into the world, and commands Seraiah <note>original: "Saraiæ." A symbolic preview or model of a future spiritual reality.</note> of the sinking of Babylon: this must be referred to the Spirit of God. It fully instructs the evangelical men <note>Referencing the "Viri Galilaei" or "Viris Evangelicos," a common Joachimite term for a future order of spiritual monks who would preach at the end of the world.</note> who are to be raised up in the mysteries hidden from the ends of the ages, so that they may reveal them to the faithful Christian peoples dispersed throughout the whole world. This serves as a sign and a memorial of those who are to be destroyed: so that if they despise repentance, they may fall under the judgment of the commonwealth, for ignorance of the word of God does not excuse them.

<margin>Isaiah 13</margin>
Isaiah wove his oracle concerning Babylon, while Jeremiah explains the word concerning Babylon in a reversed order. ## of Abbot Joachim on Jeremiah.

->In the Prologue.<-

That the three-part division of the generations of Christ, of which Matthew speaks in the first chapter, carries the type <note>original: "typum"; a symbolic model or archetype</note> of the three states of the world: namely, of the laity, the clergy, and the monks.

That the first division signifies the first state, begun from Abraham in the person of God the Father and the order of the laity, receiving its end in John the Baptist. The second division signifies the second state, begun from Christ in the person of the Son and the order of the clergy, which will have its end and departure in the Elijah who is to come before the Judgment. The third division signifies the third state, begun from our own days, in the person of the Holy Spirit and the order of the spiritual ones who contemplate the Lord, to be prolonged until the end of the age.

That it is necessary for Priests and bishops, and especially those of the Roman church, to be taken captive and to suffer at the hands of the prince of the republic <note>original: "princeps reipublicae"; referring to a secular ruler or emperor</note>.

That two orders of religious men <note>Joachim famously predicted the rise of two new preaching orders, often later identified as the Franciscans and Dominicans.</note> are to be revealed and are to come, who will shine in the stings of future tribulation through voluntary poverty and the purity of spiritual doctrine and life.

That Peter signifies the Latins <note>The Western/Catholic Church</note>, John signifies the Greeks <note>The Eastern/Orthodox Church</note>, and Mary signifies the Jews.

That the Latins believe first, the Greeks second, and the Jews third, whose remnants shall be converted; and thus the first shall be last in the second state, and the last shall be first in the third state.

->In Chapter 1.<-

That the Holy Spirit often brings forth diverse senses or understandings in the sacred scripture.

That "God" can be understood in a sevenfold relative way.

### *In the Prologue.*

That the three-part arrangement of the generations of Christ, of which Matthew speaks in the first chapter, carries the type <note>In biblical interpretation, a "type" is a person or event in the past that foreshadows something in the future.</note> of the three states of the world: namely, that of the laity, the clergy, and the monks.

That the first station signifies the first state, begun from Abraham in the person of God the Father and the order of the laity, receiving its end in John the Baptist. The second station signifies the second state, begun from Christ in the person of the Son and the order of the clergy, which will have its end and departure in the Elijah who is to come before the Judgment. The third station signifies the third state, begun from our own days, in the person of the Holy Spirit and the order of spiritual contemplatives <note>Abbot Joachim famously predicted a coming "Age of the Holy Spirit," a utopian era of monastic peace and spiritual understanding.</note> of the Lord, which is to be prolonged until the end of the age.

That it is necessary for Priests and Pontiffs, and especially those of the Roman Church, to be captured and to suffer at the hands of the prince of the state <note>original: "principe reipublicæ"; referring to a secular ruler or the "prince of the commonwealth."</note>.

That two orders of religious are to be revealed and are yet to come, who will shine through voluntary poverty and the purity of spiritual doctrine and life amidst the stings of future tribulation <note>Joachim's followers often identified these "two orders" with the Franciscans and Dominicans, who appeared shortly after his death.</note>.

That Peter signifies the Latins <note>The Western Church</note>, John signifies the Greeks <note>The Eastern Orthodox Church</note>, and Mary signifies the Jews.

That the Latins believe first, the Greeks second, and the Jews third, whose remnants shall be converted; and thus the first shall be last in the second state, and the last shall be first in the third state.

That the Holy Spirit often brings forth <note>original: "parturit"; literally "gives birth to."</note> diverse senses or understandings in Holy Scripture.

That "God" can be understood in a sevenfold relative way.

That from the aforementioned account, a typical understanding <note>original: "typicus intellectus"; in medieval theology, this refers to a symbolic or allegorical interpretation where historical events foreshadow spiritual truths.</note> is to be assigned to the three states of the human race.

What kind of prophet and truthful teacher should be, who is to be destined for the people of the nations. Where, under the name of the three tribes—namely, Judah, Benjamin, and Levi, which were collectively called "one tribe"—he is to be instructed with no small effort regarding the faith of the Trinity and the worship of the one God.

That in the aforementioned tribes, the whole Trinity is designated. For the tribe of Judah, which is royal, designates the person of the Father; the tribe of Benjamin, also royal, designates the person of the Son; and the tribe of Levi, which is priestly, designates the person of the Holy Spirit.

That the said tribes, after the other tribes were taken captive by the Assyrians, were more strongly joined together, and called entirely "one tribe," so that from then on they would be, speak, and think as one.

That the tribe of Judah signifies the Roman Church, according to the understanding pertaining to the second state <note>Joachim's "Second Age" is the era of the New Testament and the organized Church, governed by the Son.</note> of the Church; and its kings signify the high prelates and pontiffs of that same tribe.

That the tribe of Benjamin signifies the church of the clerical prelates; Levi signifies the church of contemplatives <note>monks or those dedicated to silent prayer and meditation</note>, from which spiritual teachers descend like angels from heaven to instruct the people.

That such teachers and prophets are to be sent in the near future, who will not only illuminate their subjects, but will strike even the pontiffs themselves like lightning and will not falter <note>original: "non palpitent"; literally "not throb" or "not tremble," suggesting they will speak with terrifying, unwavering authority.</note>.

That in the near future, faithful teachers and preachers are to be revealed in the Church, who will strike earthly and carnal hearts with every plague, and by their studies impose silence upon the arrogant and prideful masters.

That the future <term>order</term> <note>In Joachim's thought, the "New Order" refers to a spiritualized monastic group he believed would usher in a new age of peace and understanding.</note> designated by Jeremiah will be directed toward the obedience of the Supreme Pontiff.

That although a new order of preachers may seem to arise in the Church, the order itself was nonetheless initiated by the prophets, the apostles, and the teachers of the third time <note>The "Third Age" or "Third State" of the Holy Spirit.</note> of the Church.

### In Chapter 2.

That in the first age, the seed of Abraham <note>original: "Habraam"</note> was chosen from among all nations; in the second, the seed of Christ—that is, the apostles—was chosen from the Jews; and in the third, those to be chosen are from all of Judea and every nation, which is to say, from the entire Latin Church <note>The "Latin Church" refers to the Western, Roman Catholic Church as a whole.</note>.

That just as in the first state there were the "firstfruits" or remnants of the Israelites, and in the second state the apostles were the firstfruits of those reborn: so too now, in the beginning of the third state <term>third state: "tertij status"; in the theology of Joachim of Fiore, this is the final Age of the Holy Spirit, characterized by spiritual renewal and monastic life</term>, certain firstfruits of the Christian clergy are to be sanctified in faith by God, to be sent and scattered throughout the entire world.

That the Church, being in future pain and affliction, shall give birth to the "sons" so often mentioned—the preachers—who will bring sorrow to the clergy and the obstinate, but joy to the penitent; these are designated in the scripture: *A child is born to us, and a son is given to us* <note>original: "Puer natus est nobis, & filius datus est nobis"; a reference to Isaiah 9:6, here applied to the emergence of new religious orders</note>.

That through the aforementioned words (*a child is born to us*), and because Christ is both God and man, there shall be a twin order of two groups: one of which shall go to the "battle" of preaching and exhortation, while the other shall go to the "leisure" of singing the psalms.

That, in a moral sense, the "desert" is the soul abandoned by God, an uninhabitable land.

That in the desert of this world are the proud, the gluttonous, the lustful, and the furious: and these are represented by Oreb, Zeb, Zebah, and Zalmunna <note>original: "Oreb, Zeb, Zebeæ & Salmana"; Midianite leaders defeated by Gideon in the Book of Judges, used here as allegories for specific vices</note>.

That the fruit of the contemplatives is the joy of the spirit; the fruit of scripture is the spirit of understanding; the fruit of the reborn is salvation; the fruit of the virtues is eternal gain: these are the best merits of the Kingdom.

That God will punish the laity less than the clergy and the prelates <note>A "prelate" is a high-ranking member of the clergy, such as a bishop or abbot</note>, because the laity knew less of God’s will.

That, in a moral sense, "fornicators" are those who are bent over by vices; "adulterers" are those who, in their daily works, pull others away from the Word of God.

That the first age of the world was from Adam until Noah, when the vice of gluttony was forbidden; the second from Noah until Abraham, when it was forbidden to eat flesh with its blood; the third from Abraham (which was divided in the time of Moses) and extended until David, in which manifest circumcision was performed; the fourth from David until the Babylonian exile, in which the worship of God was expanded; the fifth from then until Christ, in which some returned to Jerusalem while others remained behind.

## In Chapter 17.

That the sin of Rome and of the whole general Church is described in the prophets and proclaimed by other prophets soon to come—namely, two <term>orders: groups of religious men, often identified in this tradition as the Franciscans and Dominicans</term>—to reveal the shame of their Mother the Church, specifically that of its prelates, clerics, and members of religious orders, through a spiritual teaching that is harsh and strong, in the style of a punishing scourge.

That although the <term>Sodomitic: referring to sexual sins associated with Sodom</term> stain was a great offense, the <term>simoniacal: the sin of buying or selling sacred things or Church offices</term> depravity of the Church is even greater. For that was the corruption for which Sodom was overthrown in an instant. How much more, then, must the Church be overthrown, which is signified by the figure of Judah? <note>Judah is frequently used in prophetic literature to represent the people of God who have fallen into hypocrisy or betrayal.</note>

That in the coming tribulation, everyone is to be plundered and scourged: the prelates, the clergy, the religious, and the laity. For everyone has transgressed, and from the greatest to the least, all are devoted to greed and other wicked deeds.

That carnal people, who love the world rather than heaven—a world in which dwell all cunning, fraud, and deceit—are unable to see what is good. Because they are blinded by temporary things, they do not perceive eternal goodness but instead grope after evil in the world. For this reason, they will dwell in a land of infernal saltness. <note>original: "falſuginis"; likely referring to the barren salt-land mentioned in Jeremiah 17:6, a symbol of spiritual desolation.</note>

That just as the partridge hatches eggs it did not lay, so the Roman Church—signified by the partridge—having a zeal for God but not according to knowledge, fosters the sect of the <term>Patarenes: a medieval group often labeled as heretics, sometimes associated with the Cathars</term> by failing to punish and uproot them from among the faithful. Therefore, when persecution breaks out in the near future, the Church will not be able to escape its traps, and it will even overthrow many of the learned and the faithful. <note>The partridge metaphor comes from Jeremiah 17:11, often interpreted in the Middle Ages as a symbol of the devil or a misguided leader stealing the "chicks" (followers) of others.</note>

What **Merlin the Briton** and the **Erythraean and Babylonian Sibyls** <note>Famed legendary prophets; their "prophecies" were frequently cited in the Middle Ages to validate apocalyptic predictions</note> say regarding the future tribulation, and how under the **second eagle** there shall be several **false popes** at the same time, by which the Church will be impoverished; these false popes shall rival the true papacy.

That it is a weakness of human distrust to trust more in man than in God; and therefore, by the just judgment of God, that from which one hopes for help shall collapse.

That resources and riches were not given for the sake of abundance in pride, but for use; therefore, he who is suddenly elevated is brought to an end in vain.

That in this **fifth ecclesiastical age** <note>In medieval historiography, the "fifth age" often referred to a period of internal trial or the time from Charlemagne to the arrival of the Antichrist</note>, in which the Church is oppressed by its own household, it ought not to boast in worldly substance, but in the power of God.

That if faithful princes have bestowed anything upon the "poor Christ" <note>Referring to the Church's property, intended to support the needy</note>, it is not fitting that the clerical order—expanded by peace, fattened by wealth, and bloated by idleness—should kick back <note>original: "recalcitret"; a metaphor of a well-fed ox kicking its master, used here to describe clerical rebellion or arrogance</note>; rather, the surplus should be given to the poor, and not to famous men and "giants" building the **Tower of Babylon**.

That **gold** was offered to Christ by the Magi, by whose help He might flee into Egypt; **myrrh**, by which He would undergo the cross <note>original: "patibulum"</note>; and **frankincense**, by which He would praise God.

That the saying of **Daniel**, chapter nine <note>Referring to the "abomination of desolation" in Daniel 9:27</note>, applies to modern prelates and rectors of the Church: namely, "When you shall see the abomination, note the explanation."

That once the Church's surrounding defenses are removed, it will incur the hardships of poverty and the squalor of public restriction.

That the iniquity of the **Latin Church** is greater than that of the **Greeks**, and therefore it shall be punished more severely.

That it is ruinous to abuse a man, but it is far more ruinous to adulterate the word of God through **heresy**.

That the **king of the Franks** <note>original: "rex Francorum"; referring to the French monarchy</note> is to be handed over into the hand of his enemies—namely, the kings of the imperial lands, or the prince of the **Germans** <note>original: "Alemanorum"</note>—and likewise the **Supreme Roman Pontiff** <note>The Pope</note> with his followers.

### In Chapter 45

That in a time of persecution and ecclesiastical affliction, or even for an overturned sinner, it is not fitting for a preacher to speak of sublime things, but rather of those things which conform to the saints; indeed, he should remain entirely silent and save himself, and reject the other who is incorrigible.

### In Chapter 46

That whatever this prophet follows here in the reading of the text is to be understood **ironically** against the Franks.
That the Franks and the Germans will convene and rise up against each other: but the army of the Franks will fall.
That there will be a schism and discord among the Franks.
That the Franks will rise up against the Franks, and **France** <note>original: "Francia"</note> will fall into the hand of the Empire.

### In Chapter 48

That the captivity of the **Greeks** <note>Referring to the Eastern Orthodox Church, often viewed by Western writers as being in "captivity" to schism or Turkish rule</note> will be converted to the faith and unity of the Roman Church, around the end of the **second state** and the beginning of the **third**, which is now imminent. <note>In the prophetic tradition of Joachim of Fiore, history is divided into three "States" or Ages: the Age of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. The "Third State" was expected to be an era of global spiritual peace.</note>

## In Chapter 50

That just as the power of the Empire will afflict and devastate other kingdoms, and especially the Church, so too will the imperial power of the **Germans** itself be devastated by all the others whom it once afflicted.

That for the sake of salvation, the Lord will soon send **evangelical men** <note>original: "viros euangelicos"; in the prophetic tradition of Joachim of Fiore, these are the "spiritual men" or new monastic orders destined to lead the Church into a new age</note> across the whole breadth of the Church, to piously foretell the end of the world’s earthly pride and to uproot the seeds of vice from human hearts.

That unless the pastors of the Church voluntarily give up their **temporal goods** <note>Wealth, land, and political power</note>, the **sword of the north** <note>original: "gladius aquilonis"; a biblical symbol of coming judgment, here identified specifically as the Holy Roman Empire</note> will be brought against them. The secular leader presiding over the state will become more cruel in his violations the more the **Supreme Pastor** <note>The Pope</note> and others remain stubborn in clinging to their worldly possessions.

That whatever the prophet says regarding the sword, famine, and plague against the Jews will surely happen to the Christian people in the coming time of affliction.

That if one person were to preside over the state, and the Christian people served him as an excellent leader, the **ship of Peter** <note>original: "Petri nauis"; a traditional metaphor for the safety and stability of the Church</note> would not easily face such ruin.

That whether the world wishes it or not, it is necessary for **pontifical pride** to fall and for the Church's focus on temporal wealth to be diminished.

That because of the ruin of the **Roman Empire**, the coming evangelical men will advise the "elect" <note>Those chosen by God for salvation</note> to withdraw from the midst of **Babylon** <note>In apocalyptic writing, Babylon represents a place of sin, exile, or the corrupted structures of the world</note>, lest they share in its eternal or temporal punishments.

## In Chapter 51

That the Holy Spirit will fully instruct the **evangelical men** <note>original: "Viros euangelicos"; in the prophetic tradition of Joachim of Fiore, these are the "spiritual men" or new monastic orders destined to lead the Church into a new age</note> who are to be raised up, regarding the mysteries hidden from the beginning of time: so that they may reveal them to the faithful Christian peoples scattered throughout the whole world, as a sign and memory for those destined for perdition; so that if they despise repentance, they may fall under the judgment of the state, as ignorance of the word of God does not excuse them.

That Isaiah and Jeremiah proceed in an opposite order as they weave the history of the exaltation and destruction of **Babylon** <note>In this prophetic context, Babylon is explicitly identified as a symbol for a corrupt **Rome**</note>.

That the **Erythraean Sibyl** <note>A legendary pagan prophetess whose verses were highly regarded by medieval Christians as foretelling the coming of Christ and the end of the world</note> says: "After these things, an **eagle** <note>A standard symbol for the Holy Roman Emperor</note> shall come having a head and feet, 60 in number, of the color of a leopard in its spots, a fox in its cunning, and a lion in its terror." Because perhaps, under the pretext of suppressing the **Patarenes** <note>A medieval movement often critical of church corruption; here the text suggests the Emperor uses their suppression as a legal excuse to move against the Church</note>, the eagle itself will walk deceitfully against the Church.

That the great evils which **Liguria** <note>A region in Northern Italy</note> and all of **Italy** will suffer will be shown more through experience than through words. For when the **Germans** <note>original: "Alemanis"</note> have been joined to him—that is, to the eagle or the **false pope** <note>original: "pseudopontifici"; a claimant to the papacy considered illegitimate or corrupt</note>—two Greek princes will also aid him. From this, the nobles of the Romans shall perish; and once the **Supreme Pontiff** <note>The Pope</note> has been consumed and the monasteries diminished, Christian worship will be extinguished.

That the **Empire of Constantinople** will return to the **Greeks**.
